svg.title: Charge an expense to an epic or a customer — SoftTrack web design mockup (#294)
svg.desc: A conference ticket is counted against the department of whoever spent it, and what it was spent on is in the description. A claim can name an epic and a customer and be marked rebillable, approval freezes both, and what an epic has cost is shown to finance admins only, from a route under /finance.
svg.text: Charge an expense to an epic or a customer
What it was spent on, as well as by whom

g.text: Finance → Expense claims, signed in as Omar
Every claim on this SoftTrack. Approval is finance’s call, not the manager chain’s;
what happens to an approved claim is Reimbursements.
Hotel, client workshop in Lisbon · 14 Sep 2026
from the teams the claimant is on
Money you spent for work and want back. Only you and finance admins see
these: an expense says where you were and what you bought.
Approved by Omar Haddad on 30 Sep 2026.
WHAT IT HAS COST, BEYOND SALARIES
From a route under /finance. Shown to finance admins only.

svg.text: The same epic, to its team

g.text: Nothing about money. The epic’s own response carries none, and
the schema sweep keeps it so.

svg.text: Done when a claim can name an epic from the claimant’s teams and a customer, both optional; a claim with a customer can be marked rebillable; approval freezes both; an epic’s
page shows approved claims charged to it per currency to finance admins only while the epic’s own response carries nothing about money; and the queue and reports filter by epic

g.text: What it was spent on was in the
description. Now it is a field.
The customer will be charged for it.
Approval freezes the epic and the
customer with the rest of the claim.
An epic that is deleted or archived leaves its name on the claims
